solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Staff penning sheep work with knotted rope

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, so the staff encloses the sheep

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A shepherd's crook holding a sheep while someone ties knotted rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is the ceremonial rod carried in processions.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is the craft of knotting cord or rope into decorative patterns.

clue.text: Daughter thrown from motorbike to sulk

indicators.note: a rider thrown from a bike is no longer on it, so the letter comes off

parts.note: a small, low-powered motorbike
D = daughter, the letter removed from the end

explanation.surface: A girl is flung off a motorbike and sulks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: MOPED loses its final D. D for daughter comes from family trees and genealogy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to brood gloomily and listlessly.

clue.text: Head across pond — caught parrot fish

parts.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
to parrot or to ape is to copy
the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the Atlantic and lands a parrotfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across pond' means across the Atlantic, so in America; 'head' is a headland. Parrot fish looks like one creature but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a headland in Massachusetts, over the pond from Britain.

clue.text: Sober group securing reduced payment for venue

indicators.note: the group holds the payment fast inside it

parts.note: AA = Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay sober
rent is a regular payment; reduced to REN

explanation.surface: A temperance society pays a deposit to hire a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober group' reads as a description of a staid gathering, but it is the recovery organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific kind: an arena is a large venue for sport or shows.

clue.text: Canines still within limits to explore the ground

indicators.note: within means inside, so still sits inside the limits of explore
the limits of a word are its first and last letters
ground as in crushed, so THE is broken up

parts.note: still = yet, as in 'not done yet'
the letters of 'the' rearranged
the first and last letters of explore

explanation.surface: Dogs snuffle around the edges of some land, exploring it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs sniffing the ground, which is exactly the picture the surface paints; here it means teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye teeth are the canine teeth of the upper jaw.

clue.text: Marine, excellent in sea, fabulous swimmer

indicators.note: the marine and excellent go inside the sea

parts.note: the Med = the Mediterranean Sea
RM = Royal Marine
A1 = excellent, with the 1 standing as I

explanation.surface: A marine soldier praises a remarkable swimmer out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable, not merely wonderful, which is why the swimmer is a creature of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a legendary sea creature, a swimmer of fable.

clue.text: Bodies taken here from doctor, loveless rascal

indicators.note: love is O in tennis scoring, so the rascal loses an O

parts.note: MO = medical officer
a rogue is a rascal; without O it is RGUE

explanation.surface: Corpses are handed over by a doctor who is an unloved scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A morgue is where dead bodies are taken and kept.

clue.text: Communist brute devouring right winger

parts.note: red = communist

indicators.note: what is devoured ends up inside the eater

parts.note: a beast is a brute
R = right

explanation.surface: A political story: a communist thug attacking a right-wing opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right winger' reads as politics, but right is just R and winger is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A redbreast is a robin, a creature with wings.

clue.text: Pull a vehicle up in race series with Tesla

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word upside down
the vehicle goes inside the race series plus Tesla

parts.note: used as is
the TT = Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
T = tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
a car is a vehicle; up it is RAC

explanation.surface: An electric car is entered into a motor race series.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car brand, but it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: a magnet that attracts iron pulls it in.

clue.text: Drained Henry late to mount in action

indicators.note: to mount is to climb, so in a down clue the word runs upward
Henry and the reversed word go inside the action

parts.note: a deed is an action
H = henry, the unit of inductance
tardy = late; mounted it is YDRAT

explanation.surface: A worn-out man called Henry arrives late to get on his horse for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a man's name, but it is the SI unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained in its literal sense: something dehydrated has had its water drawn out.

clue.text: Fellow about to lift favourite manipulative performer

indicators.note: the fellow goes round the rest

parts.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal
to up something is to lift it
the teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: A man is about to hoist his favourite showman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but the two words do separate jobs: one wraps, the other starts a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppeteer performs by manipulating puppets, so the adjective is literal.

clue.text: Wife's time in dukedom wasting years

indicators.note: the time goes inside the dukedom

parts.note: a duchy is a duke's domain; minus Y it is DUCH
T = time
Y = years

explanation.surface: A duchess passes her time on the estate as the years slip by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, short for duchess.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: Dutch is London slang for one's wife.

clue.text: Writer very naughty boy involved in Fourth Estate in France?

indicators.note: the boy is wrapped up inside the estate and fourth

parts.note: a château is a French country estate
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet
from Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'he's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy'

explanation.surface: A writer with a very naughty boy mixed up in the French press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth Estate' looks like the press, which suits a writer, but it splits into a letter and a French estate.
explanation.definitionFit: François-René de Chateaubriand was a French writer and statesman.

clue.text: Cook burned a lot — no square meals here?

indicators.note: to cook is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A cook burns so much that nobody gets a proper meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'square meal': a round table is not square, and meals are eaten there. The question mark flags that joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by joke: the table's shape is literally not square, so 'square meals' cannot be had at it.

clue.text: Stubborn alumnus expected to harbour traitor

parts.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter, so expected holds the traitor

parts.note: due = expected, as in 'the train is due'
a rat is a traitor

explanation.surface: A stubborn former pupil is expected to shelter a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy for a former pupil is a British school usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change.

clue.text: See revolutionary men box ears regularly

indicators.note: turning round, so the men are reversed

parts.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a chest is a box

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of ears is kept

parts.note: the 1st and 3rd letters of ears

explanation.surface: A revolutionary sees soldiers boxing each other's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Rochester in Kent is one. 'Revolutionary' tempts you to CHE, which is only part of the box.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is an English cathedral city and the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Repeated phrase from siren, not quiet

indicators.note: the siren is to be taken without the quiet

parts.note: a mantrap is a seductive woman, a siren
p = piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A siren wails the same phrase over and over, never quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Siren suggests an alarm, but it is the temptress of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a sacred chant; by extension any phrase said over and over.

clue.text: Author with Irish name

parts.note: and = with, as in 'fish and chips'
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language
N = name

explanation.surface: A writer with an Irish name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Irish describe the name; it is a piece of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish author of fairy tales.

clue.text: Subtlety one's sacrificed in trial

indicators.note: given up, so the letters are removed

parts.note: a trial is a nuisance, an annoyance
one = I, plus the S of 's

explanation.surface: A fine detail is lost when a courtroom trial sacrifices someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' wants to be a court case; it is a trying person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle difference in meaning or tone.

clue.text: Treat by reviving old memories of production of Cabaret

indicators.note: a new production of the word stages its letters differently

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A revival of the musical Cabaret stirs old memories.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a psychotherapy term; the capital C sells the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To abreact is to release repressed emotion by reliving the experience, as in therapy.

clue.text: Where one batter differs from another for example?

definitions.text: Where one batter differs from another
definitions.meaning: a cryptic definition: think of how batters stand at the crease or plate
a plain synonym, used in 'for example'

explanation.surface: Comparing two batsmen, perhaps in cricket or baseball.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN STANCE: that is where two batters differ. 'For example' is a nod to 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Interchangeable in the stock phrase: 'for example' and 'for instance' say the same thing.

clue.text: French milk double entendre recalled about marriage

indicators.note: called back, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: lait is French for milk
a pun plays on two meanings

explanation.surface: A saucy joke about French milk is remembered at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string is reversed at once, so the second piece ends up first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is the adjective for marriage and weddings, so 'about marriage' works as a descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Harry Maguire leaving United an illusion

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are knocked about
whatever is leaving departs the word, so United's letter goes

parts.note: anagram fodder, less the U
U = United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Footballer Harry Maguire leaving Manchester United is a false hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Maguire is a real England defender who played for Manchester United, so 'Harry' reads as his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is the best-known optical illusion, water seen shimmering in a desert.

clue.text: Pressure to vote here — help win it corruptly

indicators.note: corrupted letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A plea to voters to help win by foul means.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-line whip is the strictest order from a British party to its MPs to vote as told.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip puts heavy pressure on MPs to vote with their party.

clue.text: Crowd in road earth mover crosses

indicators.note: the earth mover lies across the road, around it

parts.note: a hoe moves earth
Rd = road

explanation.surface: A crowd stands in the road as a digger crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth mover' suggests a bulldozer, but a garden hoe moves earth too.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though a horde suggests a crowd that is large and unruly.

clue.text: Muslim festival involving new Celtic goddess

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
N = new

explanation.surface: A religious festival that features a new goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: N = new is standard shorthand, as in NT for New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a figure of Welsh legend, often counted as a Celtic goddess.

clue.text: Enjoyable time when filling sandwich

indicators.note: the word is the filling in the sandwich

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
as = when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A good time spent making sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' reads as sandwich filling in the surface, and that is exactly how the container works.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal usage: 'we had a blast' means we had a great time.

clue.text: Claim fool replaces former partner in strenuous work

indicators.note: one piece goes in where another comes out

parts.note: an ass is a fool; it goes in
an ex is a former partner; it comes out
exertion is strenuous effort

explanation.surface: A fool takes over from someone's ex in a hard job.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap happens at the front of the word, where the ex sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: to make a claim is to make an assertion, a statement put forward as true.

clue.text: Goddess missing knight, having no sex games

parts.note: neuter = sexless; missing N it is EUTER
N = knight in chess notation
PE = physical education, games at school

explanation.surface: A goddess without her knight and no sex, only games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing knight' sits between the definition and the thing it acts on, which hides where the definition ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is the Greek Muse of music, a minor goddess.

clue.text: Provoked Scots hooligan was in van around east

parts.note: a ned is a young Scottish tearaway
E = east
to be in the van (vanguard) is to lead

explanation.surface: A Glasgow thug in a van driving east was riled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle but means the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke them.
